title: Taylor Swift Returns to the CMA Awards Stage — Her First Performance There in 13 Years
excerpt: Taylor Swift will perform at the 60th CMA Awards on Nov. 18 in Nashville — her first time singing on the CMA stage since 2013, and her first appearance there in 10 years.
content:
Taylor Swift is coming back to where her story started. The Country Music Association and ABC announced Friday, November 13, that Swift will perform at the 60th Annual CMA Awards on Wednesday, November 18, live from Bridgestone Arena in Nashville — her first performance on the CMA Awards stage in 13 years.

The announcement landed on Friday the 13th, a fitting date for a singer who has long called 13 her lucky number. The ceremony airs live from 8 to 11 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+, streaming the next day on Hulu.

Thirteen years since “Red”

Swift last sang at the CMA Awards on November 6, 2013, when she performed an acoustic version of “Red” with Alison Krauss and Vince Gill. That night she also received the Pinnacle Award. She returned to the ceremony in 2016, but only to present — handing the Entertainer of the Year Award to Garth Brooks. Her performance next Wednesday will be her first appearance at the show in 10 years, and her first time singing on its stage in 13.

Swift first attended the CMA Awards in 2006 and won her first CMA Award in 2007, the Horizon Award, now known as New Artist of the Year. She has since taken home the Entertainer of the Year Award twice, and has delivered eight performances across seven CMA Awards ceremonies.

A nominee, not just a guest

Swift is not returning as a nostalgia act. She is nominated this year for Single of the Year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the original song she wrote for the Disney and Pixar film Toy Story 5 and produced with Jack Antonoff. It is her 26th career CMA nomination and her first at the show since 2022. The song recently reached No. 1 on U.S. country radio — her first song to top that chart in 13 years.

What she will sing on November 18 has not been announced, and no collaborators have been confirmed for the performance.

The 60th anniversary show

The milestone ceremony will be hosted by Lainey Wilson for a third consecutive year. Swift joins a performer lineup that includes Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Kacey Musgraves, Luke Combs, Megan Moroney, Miranda Lambert, the Red Clay Strays, Tim McGraw, Tucker Wetmore, Vince Gill and Zach Top. The show will also include a tribute to Dolly Parton and a tribute to Brooks & Dunn, this year’s recipients of the CMA Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award.

Swift confirmed in September, in an Instagram Stories post, that she would attend the ceremony. “LOOKS LIKE I HAVEN’T YEE’D MY LAST HAW THANK YOU CMA!!!! See you there Nov. 18,” she wrote at the time.

What it means

Analysis: the return closes a circle Swift has been drawing all year. “I Knew It, I Knew You” brought her back to country radio’s summit for the first time in 13 years, and now the CMA stage — the room where she won her first award as a teenager — gives that comeback its biggest platform. For country fans in Laredo and the 956, Wednesday night is appointment viewing: the genre’s biggest star, back on its biggest night, in the city where it all began for her.
